description: crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs: SetErrorType::Display uses a wildcard arm '_ => return write\!(f, "{:?}", self)' guarded by #[allow(unreachable_patterns)]. The comment explains this is because the type is #[non_exhaustive]. However, this wildcard arm means any new variant added without a corresponding match arm silently falls back to Debug format instead of failing to compile, defeating the purpose of the explicit match. The idiomatic approach for a #[non_exhaustive] Display impl in the defining crate is to simply add the new variant's arm — the crate that defines the enum is not subject to non_exhaustive restrictions. The allow suppresses a warning that would catch missing arms. crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs does NOT have this pattern (its SetErrorType Display is exhaustive and correct); the mail-server should match that style.
title: SetErrorType::Display match with #[allow(unreachable_patterns)] workaround
